themes: Renewals of application maintenance, testing and BPO work carry 'forward productivity'; Wipro says traditional IT and BPO budgets are 'getting compressed' (Jul-2026). Brokers estimate 2-3% a year of revenue deflation.
New AI work (data, agents, AI governance, AI data centres)
Wipro calls it 'Reimagine AI' and says margins are better; it discloses no AI revenue (TCS: $2.6 bn run-rate; HCLTech: $171 mn a quarter).
Discretionary spend slow, decisions longer; US 10-year yield ~4.8-5.0% and a Fed hike on 16-Sep-2026; oil above $100 on the West Asia conflict.
$100,000 H-1B fee extended by a year (Sep-2026); new $4,000 H-1B / $4,500 L-1 fees from 9-Sep-2026. Wipro is ~60% offshore, so the direct cost is limited, but onsite delivery gets dearer.
Large deals keep coming (Wipro FY26 large deals $7.8 bn, +45% CC) but are priced competitively and start at low margins.
Realised Rs87.9/$ in FY26, Rs93.5 in Q1FY27, Rs94.5 in the Q2 guide: rupee revenue grows ~6-7 pp faster than dollar revenue in FY27 and lifts margins.
GCCs (clients' own captive centres in India)
Clients insource work; Wipro cited insourcing at a BFSI client (resolved by Q1FY27).

price.fact: Nifty IT peaked at ~46,000 in Dec-2024; touched 26,426 intraday on 30-Jun-2026, ~42% below the peak.
Nifty IT -27% in Jan-Sep 2026 (Nifty 50 -13%), -11.2% in September alone.
4-Feb-2026: Nifty IT -6% in a day after Anthropic's Claude Cowork plugins; Feb-2026 the index's worst month in ~23 years (Reuters: application services are 40-70% of IT firms' revenue).
19-Jun-2026: Nifty IT -6.5% after Accenture cut its FY26 constant-currency guidance to 3-4% and Q3 bookings fell ~2%.

Sep-2026: US 10-year ~4.8-5.0%, Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% (16-Sep), H-1B fee extension (21-Sep); Wipro hit 52-week lows of Rs166.3 (10-Sep) and Rs163.4 (21-Sep) and was removed from the Nifty 50 on 30-Sep (passive outflow ~$225 mn).
Motilal Oswal: tier-I IT trades 30-40% below its long-term average P/E; cheapness alone unlikely to drive a re-rating.

ownership.notes: In FY26 the Azim Premji Trust's stake fell from 10.15% to 6.49% as shares moved to the three family partnerships and Prazim Trading (intra-group). Promoters tendered ~42.8 cr shares in the Jun-2026 buyback (72.52% before, 72.59% after). DIIs fell from 7.86% (Mar-26) to 5.22% (Jun-26) and public holders rose from 11.08% to 13.21%; shareholder count jumped 17% to 30.4 lakh (retail buying around the buyback). Promoters' free float is small: public float ~27%, which is why index weights are low.

moat: Client stickiness
Moderate
97-99% of revenue from existing clients; 714 clients above $1 mn; top client 4.4%, top 10 23.6%.
Revenue is recurring, but stickiness has not stopped three years of decline.
Scale
Weak
IT Services $10.5 bn vs TCS ~$30 bn, Infosys ~$20 bn; $100 mn+ clients fell from 22 (FY24) to 16.
Less able to fund AI platforms and win mega-deals than the top two.
Consulting and domain (Capco)
Moderate
Capco gives BFSI consulting access; BFSI is 34% of revenue but Wipro's BFSI grew 0% over eight quarters (Choice).
A real asset that has not yet translated into growth.
Delivery cost and margins
Parity / weak
IT Services EBIT 16-17% vs ~21-25% at TCS/Infosys/HCLTech (Screener EBITDA margins FY26: Wipro 19.2%, TCS 27.1%, Infosys 23.7%, HCLTech 20.6%).
No cost advantage; margins are the industry's lower half.
AI positioning
Unproven
Wipro Intelligence (WINGS, WEGA), AI-native unit (Apr-2026), Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships; no AI revenue disclosed.
Peers disclose AI revenue; Wipro asks investors to take it on trust.
Management stability
Weak
Three CEOs since 2016 (Pallia since Apr-2024); strategy and go-to-market structure recast each time.
Execution risk is higher than at peers.
Balance sheet
Strong
Net cash ~Rs21,400 cr after the buyback (Screener basis, Jun-26); OCF 98-113% of net income.
Pays dividends and buybacks; no financial risk.
critiques: Wipro lags peers in every cycle: FY24-26 constant-currency revenue fell 4.4%, 2.3% and 1.6% while Infosys and HCLTech grew; Q2FY27 guidance implies organic decline.
ICICI Securities, HDFC Institutional, MOSL (Jul-2026); Centrum (Reuters, 16-Jul-2026)
AI deflation hits Wipro's book harder: application management, infrastructure and BPO-style run work is a large part of revenue, and renewals carry productivity give-backs.
The margin band (17-17.5%) is out of reach while the company invests in AI and ramps low-margin cost-takeout deals.
Bookings are volatile and fell 32% YoY in Q1FY27; large-deal conversion keeps slipping into later quarters.
The stock is cheap (below -2 SD on forward P/E; ~5% dividend yield) and the buyback shows capital discipline.
AI expands the market (agent orchestration, sovereign AI, AI governance); Europe and APMEA are growing.
